name: Conceptual Physics Notes Course Profile
role: Current Physics-specific Notes contract. Notes are built in one pass from the finalized Bank Notes anchors plus the Framework-declared textbook/source spine. The established Algebra-compatible Notes HTML/CSS shell is reused exactly; Physics specializes source density, visual continuity, Reading Apprenticeship processing, and formula/relationship treatment.

bank_canonical.rule: Finalized Unit Bank owns canonical WTC / Notes Example / Notes YTI wording, values, figures, solutions, IDs, pair identity, question-structure identity, and I-can identity.
bank_canonical.pair_rule: Use every complete canonical Example/YTI pair actually present, with no more than four canonical pairs per section under the current Physics Bank-v2 profile.
bank_canonical.display_numbering_rule: Bank IDs/pair IDs remain hidden provenance. Visible Example/You Try It numbering is assigned from final display order within the section and runs 1, 2, 3... even when Bank pair_number differs.

source_spine.rule: The Framework-declared Physics textbook/source is the instructional spine. Preserve its major conceptual order, terminology, physics meaning, and usable instructional image order. Notes may summarize/condense substantially to fit classroom time; paragraph-level fidelity is not required.
source_spine.time_target: Approximately 30–40 minutes for the complete student Notes section, including WTC, skim, reading, processing, Example/YTI work, and close.
source_spine.condense_rule: Cut repetition/tangents first, then compress prose and combine nearby explanatory paragraphs while preserving conceptual transitions. Do not delete canonical WTC or complete Example/YTI pairs merely to hit the time target.
source_spine.gap_rule: Documented source gaps remain explicit. Use only the minimum Framework-grounded bridge needed for an uncovered target; do not invent fake textbook continuation.

architecture: exact Learning Target + exact I-can statements
Vocabulary / Key Notation Preview using terms outside a 3-column one-row sort table
canonical What's to Come using the established WTC shell
Let's Get Started skim using the exact Physics notice/wonder wording and two row-based writing rows
one blue Close Reading directions annotation box
substantial summarized textbook/source reading compartmentalized by exact I-can focus while preserving source order
at most one primary processing event per reading boundary, with every substantial reading block followed by one
canonical Example / You Try It anchors, with any leftover intact pairs after the final reading
Vocabulary with definitions/reference immediately before Summary
Framework-defined final miscellaneous workspace when required

opening.vocabulary_preview_rule: Render preview terms in a visible vocab-list outside the sort table. The sort table has exactly three columns — Know for sure, Recognize, Don't know yet — and exactly one blank writing row.
opening.skim_prompt: Skim before close reading. Look at the headings and figures. Find 1–2 things you notice and 1–2 things you wonder about.
opening.skim_table_rule: Use two row-based writing rows only: What I noticed and What I wonder. Do not render Notice/Wonder as side-by-side columns.
opening.prediction_rule: Do not add a prediction prompt unless the current Framework explicitly requires it.
opening.close_reading_visual_rule: Use the deployed blue close-reading-instructions annotation box, not a standalone giant h2 section.

reading.benchmark: Framework-declared Physics textbook / approved source spine, supported by Conceptual Physics/Hewitt visual/reference resources
reading.rule: Physics Notes are textbook-like instructional reading, not thin blurbs between problems. Summarize and condense for classroom use while preserving source concept order and correct physics.
reading.i_can_compartment_rule: Every exact section I-can must headline at least one major reading block using the established notes-ican-start / notes-ican-heading shell. Preserve source order rather than reorganizing concepts artificially.
reading.vocabulary_rule: Vocabulary develops in context. Emphasize the first meaningful introduction/definition of a previewed term; do not bold every recurrence.
reading.paragraphs: multiple short developed paragraphs; avoid walls of text and one-sentence stacking

processing_rhythm.hard_rule: At a reading boundary, use at most ONE primary student-processing event: Stop and Discuss OR one canonical Example/YTI pair. Every substantial reading block must be followed immediately by one primary processing event before the next major application; short transitional/support paragraphs may have none.
processing_rhythm.instructional_insertions: Physics Notes, source figures, diagrams, graphs, models, Formula / Relationship blocks, and other explanatory references may be embedded with the reading when they teach the idea; they are not a second primary student-processing event.
processing_rhythm.leftover_pair_rule: If canonical Example/YTI pairs remain after all natural reading insertion points are used, place the remaining intact pairs after the final reading chunk in display order.

stop_and_discuss.count_rule: One Stop and Discuss block contains 2–4 short prompts; default to 3, use 2 for a narrow reading, and use 4 only when every prompt earns its place.
required_prompt_mix: at least one vocabulary/notation question tied to a term just used in the immediately preceding reading
at least one conceptual/representation question requiring explanation, comparison, interpretation, critique, or connection from the immediately preceding reading/figure/model
stop_and_discuss.shell_rule: Use notes-discuss-task wrapper; colored stop-discuss prompt box contains the ordered list only; the notes-ws writing workspace is a sibling OUTSIDE the colored box and remains plain white space.
stop_and_discuss.hewitt_source: Think and Discuss / Think and Explain / Think and Rank structures are preferred inspiration when they fit.

visual_storytelling.source_image_rule: Use every usable instructional image/figure present in the declared student-source section, in source order. Exclude only navigation/decorative chrome, answer-key-only visuals, or images that directly leak a student answer.
visual_storytelling.size_rule: Default maximum displayed image height is 4 inches with width auto, max-width 100%, preserved aspect ratio, and centered presentation. Increase only a genuinely unreadable labeled figure as needed, normally to 5 inches and never beyond 6 inches without a clear reason.
visual_storytelling.no_crude_redraw: Never replace a good source/canonical figure with a crude redraw.

formula_relationship.rule: When an important physical/mathematical relationship is first introduced, render a compact Formula / Relationship reference block using the established math-notes header/body visual shell.
do_not: turn Notes into a detached formula sheet
repeat the same relationship box at every recurrence
present an equation as an answer machine

task_shell.workspace_rule: For each notes-task, notes-task-content contains the heading/prompt/representation and notes-ws notes-task-workspace is a sibling immediately after notes-task-content.

reading_apprenticeship.rule: Keep annotation, vocabulary noticing, notice/wonder, evidence, model-reading, and representation interpretation opportunities purposeful; student workspaces may be generous for Notability.

student_teacher.student: clean Notability-first page with generous fixed workspace where required; use established keep-together wrappers and natural pagination
student_teacher.teacher: same instructional sequence, browser-only; fixed student workspace heights are released; teacher support expands naturally downward with no print/page-fit optimization; answers/acceptable reasoning are scannable bulleted lists; Teacher Moves and Student Moves are separate labeled lists; no overlap. Vertical space is not a concern.

teacher_support.browser_only_rule: Teacher Notes are browser-only. Release fixed student workspaces and let teacher support expand naturally; do not optimize teacher guides for print/page fit.
teacher_support.visual_rule: Match the established Algebra Notes teacher-guide convention: teacher-only answers/guidance/discourse are inside a red, bold wrapper using ordinary paragraph/list elements. Do not rely on h4 headings because base CSS renders h4 navy.
teacher_support.wtc_rule: Every WTC gets Answer / Acceptable Reasoning, Teacher Moves, Student Moves, and Listen For when useful. Multipart answers use one bullet per labeled part.
teacher_support.stop_and_discuss_rule: Every Stop and Discuss gets numbered acceptable reasoning matching its 2–4 prompts, plus content-specific Teacher Moves and Student Moves; add Listen For when useful.
teacher_support.example_yti_rule: Every Example and every YTI gets its own canonical answer/solution plus Teacher Moves and Student Moves. Add Listen For when the item has a meaningful likely error.
preferred_order: Listen For / Likely Misconception when useful

pagination.student_rule: Student Notes are Notability-first. Use the established Notes/base CSS wrappers and keep atomic instructional units together when practical. Do not wrap a giant multi-page reading in one avoid-break container.
pagination.student_forced_break_rule: Do not use forced page breaks for ordinary student-layout crowding repair. Use them only for a genuinely intentional separate student page/workspace required by the current Framework/shell.
pagination.teacher_rule: Teacher Notes are browser-only. Do not preserve student pagination or add teacher-only forced page breaks.
